fact: Camtel operates four existing submarine cables for Cameroon (SAIL, WACS, SAT-3 and NCSCS, the Nigeria-Cameroon cable), with 2024 utilisation of 6%, 57%, 29% and 92% respectively per a Chamber of Accounts report of June 2024, as reported by Ecofin (article of 2025-12-10; landing stations not named).
L'Economie reports that the October 2025 internet disruption in Cameroon was attributed to a problem on the WACS submarine cable, described as the cable that links the country to the global network.
MINPOSTEL's Secretary General reported that in 2025 Camtel raised the capacity of the NCSCS submarine cable from 100 Gbps to 300 Gbps, with a study towards 2.4 Tbps.

Xalam Analytics states that Cameroon is connected to four submarine cables offering direct routes to Europe, South Africa and the Americas; the cables and landing stations are not named in the passages.

AFR-IX telecom states that the Ceiba-2 submarine cable (400 km, 40 Gbps, built Oct 2015 to Mar 2017) connects Malabo, Bata and Kribi in Cameroon, and Equatorial Guinea inaugurated its link to it on 4 June 2018; as_of is the inauguration date.
